rendered_text:
# Blue Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Blue

**Tagline:** Possibility opens when the pattern is understood.

**Mana alignment:** W: 1, U: 10, B: 1, R: 1, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The measured trace - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Blue and Black.
- Signal 2: Become the changed thing - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed Blue and Quandrix College.
- Signal 3: Map the variables - You preferred making the table answer you before comfort became a plan. It echoed Blue and Azorius Senate.
- Signal 4: Improve the model - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Blue and Simic Combine.

## Commander Path

Blue wants a Commander deck that turns knowledge into control: draw cards, preserve options, answer key spells, and let information become inevitability. Start with Draw-Go Control or Spellslinger Tokens, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Control, Aggro.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Card draw, counterspells, bounce, copy effects, artifact engines, and spellslinger lines that make every option feel planned.

## Table Caution

Hold mana for the important spell, draw before committing, and keep one clean answer for the table's real threat.

## Archetypes

- Draw-Go Control: Hold mana, gather cards, answer threats on the stack, and win once the table runs out of clean openings.
- Spellslinger Tokens: Turn instants and sorceries into repeatable pressure while keeping interaction available.
- Artifacts and Clones: Use tools, copies, and engines to turn observed structures into your own advantage.

## Card Signals

### Creatures

- Baral, Chief of Compliance
- Talrand, Sky Summoner
- Consecrated Sphinx

### Instants and Sorceries

- Ponder

## Mana Notes

### Basic mana note
Tune Islands to your early pips after the nonbasic shell, ramp package, and utility lands are chosen.

## Commander Browsing Notes

- Talrand, Sky Summoner (Current Scryfall-Verified Support): Turns Blue's patient instant-speed posture into a visible board of evasive threats. Skip if: You want hard artifact engines or wizard tribal more than spell-based token pressure. Skip if: You want a classic counterspell deck instead of a draw-trigger creature plan. rendered_text:
# House Dimir Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** House Dimir

**Tagline:** Secrets, backroom deals, and hidden information leverage.

**Mana alignment:** W: 1, U: 10, B: 10, R: 1, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The cold pattern - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed House Dimir and Black.
- Signal 2: Become the changed thing - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed House Dimir and Quandrix College.
- Signal 3: Hold it until timing matters - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It was answered by House Dimir.
- Signal 4: Keep the secret - You kept value in what the table could not yet see. It was answered by House Dimir.

## Commander Path

House Dimir wants a Commander deck that wins once the table understands too late: trade in hidden information, mill or discard the right resources, and turn the delayed payoff into a protected finish. Start with Hidden Information Leverage or Surveil Texture, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Graveyard, Aggro.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Surveil, discard, mill, evasive threats, theft, and control tools that reward patience and secrecy over noise.

## Table Caution

Wait until shields drop, hold interaction, and draw cards before revealing the card that actually wins.

## Archetypes

- Hidden Information Leverage: Use Dimir when secrecy, backroom positioning, observation, and selective disclosure lead over generic UB mechanics.
- Surveil Texture: Use surveil as source-backed information filtering, not as a claim that mill or graveyard gameplay defines the guild.
- Public-Surface Guardrail: Keep Dimir adjacent when the answer is mainly public law, visible obligation, spectacle, rhetoric, or biological optimization.

## Card Signals

- None listed

### Basic mana note
Tune Islands and Swamps to your early pips after the nonbasic shell, ramp package, and utility lands are chosen.

## Commander Browsing Notes

- Lazav, Dimir Mastermind (Native Fit): Auxiliary product fit for players who want a Lazav-led Dimir deck; the canonical proof is Lazav as guildmaster, not the deck mechanics. Skip if: you want a transparent table plan or a commander whose appeal does not depend on opponents' graveyards. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/znc/92/lazav-dimir-mastermind) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/lazav-dimir-mastermind)
- Etrata, the Silencer (Weird Stretch): Auxiliary product texture for the assassin side of the official Dimir overview; it is not a source-backed key-figure proof chain in this packet. Skip if: you do not want a commander that repeatedly leaves combat and can be mechanically awkward. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/grn/170/etrata-the-silencer) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/etrata-the-silencer)

name: Simic Combine
decree: Simic Combine recognizes the shape of your game as The Adaptive Biodesigner. Your answers repeatedly expressed measured inference and transformative cost. Bant stayed near the reading, but Simic Combine was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary guild fit.
hero: Simic read you as someone who expects a living plan to change. Green supplies the organism; blue supplies the method. Together, the deck asks what the next version can become. Bant stayed close because your answers also carried public honor, refined protection, living support, communal trust, and champion responsibility. The deciding difference was how Simic turns that pressure into incremental growth, biological scaling, and threats that outgrow old answers.
reading_signal: Simic Combine led with a moderate signal. A secondary signal stayed close: Bant suggested public honor, refined protection, living support, communal trust, and champion responsibility, while this result centered adaptation, growth, and biological change. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves forward into adaptation and upgrade.

# Simic Combine Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Simic Combine

**Tagline:** Life studied as an adaptive, improvable system.

**Mana alignment:** W: 4, U: 9, B: 4, R: 3, G: 10

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The measured trace - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Simic Combine and Black.
- Signal 2: Become the changed thing - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed Simic Combine and Quandrix College.
- Signal 3: Adapt the organism - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It was answered by Simic Combine.
- Signal 4: Run the experiment - You preferred making the table answer you before comfort became a plan. It was answered by Izzet League.

## Commander Path

Simic Combine wants a Commander deck that adapts in motion: ramp, evolve through counters, and turn biological upgrades into flash-value pressure that improves whenever the game changes. Start with Living-System Value or Biological Adaptation, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Ramp, Counters Matter.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Adapt and evolve creatures, counter engines, ramp, flash threats, and card draw that turn each upgrade into a larger organism.

## Table Caution

Protect the engine, draw cards after each upgrade, and rebuild with counters when removal interrupts the experiment.

## Archetypes

- Living-System Value: Ramp, card draw, and creature scale are Commander-adjacent tools; they need organism-level adaptation context before they read as Simic identity.
- Biological Adaptation: +1/+1 counters, evolve, graft, proliferate, mutate, and Adapt are texture only unless they express source-bounded biological improvement.
- Clade Research And Pressure Response: Creature experimentation fits Simic when it stays tied to clades, medicine, living systems, and adaptation under pressure.

rendered_text:
# Izzet League Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Izzet League

**Tagline:** Invent first. Stabilize what the experiment teaches.

**Mana alignment:** W: 1, U: 10, B: 1, R: 10, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The live spark - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Izzet League and Red.
- Signal 2: Become the changed thing - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed Izzet League and Quandrix College.
- Signal 3: The mechanism - You accepted volatility when it meant the table had to react on your terms. It was answered by Izzet League.
- Signal 4: Make it a test - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It was answered by Izzet League.

## Commander Path

Izzet League wants a Commander deck that turns velocity into advantage: chain experiments, recur the right spell, and use tempo to make the table answer your storm before it stabilizes. Start with Tempo / Delver or Storm, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Tempo, Spellslinger.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Cantrips, spellslinger payoffs, jump-start style recursion, storm lines, and cheap interaction that make volatile advantage repeatable.

## Table Caution

Wait for shields to drop, hold interaction, and protect the engine before you commit the storm turn.

## Archetypes

- Storm: Chain rituals and cantrips until a Storm spell copies itself enough times to kill the table in one turn.

## Card Signals

### Creatures

- Arclight Phoenix
- Murktide Regent
- Goblin Electromancer

### Instants and Sorceries

- Lightning Bolt
- Counterspell
- Faithless Looting

### Enchantments and Artifacts

- Rhystic Study
- Thousand-Year Storm

## Mana Notes

### Premium picks
- Steam Vents

- Sulfur Falls
- Riverglide Pathway
- Temple of Epiphany

### Midrange picks
- Spirebluff Canal

### Budget picks
- Izzet Guildgate

### Utility picks
- Command Tower
- Exotic Orchard
- Myriad Landscape

### Basic mana note
Tune Islands and Mountains to your early pips after the nonbasic shell, ramp package, and utility lands are chosen.

## Commander Browsing Notes

- Niv-Mizzet, Parun (Native Fit): He is the cleanest native Izzet bridge: a Ravnican Izzet leader whose gameplay rewards instant/sorcery exchanges with cards and turns card draw into precise damage. Skip if: your table dislikes compact draw-damage combos, repeated triggers, or commanders that become the whole deck plan. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/otc/235/niv-mizzet-parun) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/niv-mizzet-parun)
- Melek, Izzet Paragon (Native Fit): Melek preserves the lab-experiment feel without defaulting to the dragon. Revealing the top card and copying spells feels like an unstable experiment becoming repeatable technique. Skip if: you want a low-curve commander or dislike playing with the top of your library revealed. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/cmm/345/melek-izzet-paragon) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/melek-izzet-paragon)
- Niv-Mizzet, Dracogenius (Iconic Lore-Forward): This is a slower, more table-readable way to center Niv-Mizzet as Izzet identity: intellect, fire, and repeatable resource conversion. Skip if: you need modern efficiency or want the strongest Niv-Mizzet Commander option. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/c17/184/niv-mizzet-dracogenius) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/niv-mizzet-dracogenius)

name: White
decree: White recognizes the shape of your game as The Shelter Architect. Your answers repeatedly expressed preserving duty and shelter through structure. Boros Legion stayed near the reading, but White was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary color fit.
hero: White read you as someone who does not confuse kindness with drift. It wants protection to become structure, and structure to remain trustworthy when the room gets dangerous. Boros Legion stayed close because your answers also carried protection, grievance, and immediate action. The deciding difference was how White turns that pressure into reliable protection, disciplined pressure, and structure that keeps returning to the board.
reading_signal: White led with a strong signal. A secondary signal stayed close: Boros Legion suggested protection, grievance, and immediate action, while this result centered safety, duty, and standards that hold under pressure. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves upward into shelter and enforceable duty.

adjacentFit.relationshipCopy: Both paths recognized the same tension, but they solve it differently. White asks: "What structure still protects people when goodwill is not enough?" Boros asks: "What line was crossed, and who must answer for it?" White moves upward into shelter and enforceable duty; Boros moves outward into intervention.

# White Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** White

**Tagline:** Safety is built, not assumed.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 1, B: 1, R: 1, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The unlit edge - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It was answered by Colorless.
- Signal 2: Preserve what must not break - You trusted patience that keeps the next generation alive after the first pressure breaks. It echoed White and Boros Legion.
- Signal 3: Build the shelter - You made room for the board to become stronger together than any single card alone. It echoed White and Selesnya Conclave.
- Signal 4: Strengthen what protects - You trusted patience that keeps the next generation alive after the first pressure breaks. It echoed White and Azorius Senate.

## Commander Path

White wants a Commander deck that builds protection into the table state: widen the board, defend the key piece, and let structure turn survival into pressure. Start with Protective Tokens or Taxes and Rules, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Tokens, Control.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Token makers, protection spells, taxes, clean removal, and equipment lines that make safety feel enforceable instead of decorative.

## Table Caution

Protect the engine, keep the standards clear, and do not spend your last shield before the table commits its real threat.

## Archetypes

- Protective Tokens: Build a resilient board, widen the field, and make combat answer shared protection.
- Taxes and Rules: Set costs, slow greedy lines, and force the table to play through standards.
- Equipment and Guardians: Suit up one clean threat, protect it, and turn structure into pressure.

name: Orzhov Syndicate

golden_questions.answer_title: The claim no one can make for me

decree: Orzhov Syndicate recognizes the shape of your game as The Obligation Architect. Your answers repeatedly expressed preserving duty and debt as relationship. Yore / Artifice stayed near the reading, but Orzhov Syndicate was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary guild fit.
hero: Orzhov read you as someone who notices what is owed. White gives the institution; black gives the pressure. Together, the deck turns every exchange into a contract the table did not read closely enough. Yore / Artifice stayed close because your answers also carried engineered agency, artifice, civilization, progress, and refusal to let natural limits become final. The deciding difference was how Orzhov turns that pressure into transactional pressure, slow drain, and resource exchanges that stop being equal.
reading_signal: Orzhov Syndicate led with a strong signal. A secondary signal stayed close: Yore / Artifice suggested engineered agency, artifice, civilization, progress, and refusal to let natural limits become final, while this result centered obligation, debt, and consequence. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves downward into debt and permanence.

adjacentFit.heading: Yore / Artifice
adjacentFit.relationshipCopy: Both paths recognized the same tension, but they solve it differently. Orzhov asks: "What is owed, and who pays when the bill arrives?" Yore asks: "What limit is worth rebuilding so choice can continue?" Orzhov moves downward into debt and permanence; Yore moves toward artifice, constructed continuity, and engineered agency.

rendered_text:
# Orzhov Syndicate Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Orzhov Syndicate

**Tagline:** Debt, deals, and hierarchy made official.

**Mana alignment:** W: 9, U: 2, B: 10, R: 2, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The cold pattern - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed Orzhov Syndicate and Black.
- Signal 2: Preserve what must not break - You trusted patience that keeps the next generation alive after the first pressure breaks. It echoed Orzhov Syndicate and White.
- Signal 3: A debt that outlasts apology - You measured survival by whether the house could carry its family duty forward. It was answered by Orzhov Syndicate.
- Signal 4: Make it a debt - You made room for the board to become stronger together than any single card alone. It was answered by Orzhov Syndicate.

## Commander Path

Orzhov Syndicate wants a Commander deck that makes every exchange a debt: tax resources, drain life, sacrifice small pieces, and make obligation a pressure engine no opponent can ignore. Start with Obligation Engines or Payment Pressure, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Sacrifice, Aggro.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Afterlife bodies, aristocrats engines, extort-style drains, taxes, and recursion that make death and payment part of the same ledger.

## Table Caution

Hold a sacrifice outlet, buy time with drains, and remove the key piece before debts turn into a board wipe.

## Archetypes

- Obligation Engines: Sacrifice or death-trigger shells can be Orzhov-flavored only when framed as contract, repayment, afterlife texture, or institutional leverage rather than automatic lore proof.
- Payment Pressure: Taxing, drain, and control cards are Commander texture; they need debt, deal, payment, or hierarchy framing before they become Orzhov-adjacent.
- Afterlife Tokens: Spirit or token play echoes Orzhov only when tied to afterlife mechanics and obligation context, not all death or spirit decks.

## Card Signals

### Creatures

- Blood Artist
- Tidehollow Sculler
- Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

### Instants and Sorceries

- Thoughtseize
- Path to Exile
- Vindicate

### Enchantments and Artifacts

- Phyrexian Arena
- Grasp of Fate

## Mana Notes

### Premium picks
- Godless Shrine

- Isolated Chapel
- Brightclimb Pathway
- Temple of Silence

### Midrange picks
- Concealed Courtyard

### Budget picks
- Orzhov Guildgate
- Orzhov Basilica

### Utility picks
- Command Tower
- Exotic Orchard
- Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth
- Myriad Landscape

### Basic mana note
Tune Plains and Swamps to your early pips after the nonbasic shell, ramp package, and utility lands are chosen.

## Commander Browsing Notes

- Teysa Karlov (Native Fit): Teysa is the clearest native Orzhov product fit: she doubles death-trigger value and turns token bodies into a more threatening spiritual workforce. Skip if: you dislike sacrifice loops, death-trigger stacks, or incremental value engines. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/cmm/359/teysa-karlov) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/teysa-karlov)
- Teysa, Orzhov Scion (Native Fit): This version of Teysa strongly expresses Orzhov transaction logic: sacrifice, death, replacement bodies, and exile removal all feed the same contract engine. Skip if: you want a simple precon-style gameplan or dislike combo-adjacent sacrifice engines. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/rvr/233/teysa-orzhov-scion) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/teysa-orzhov-scion)
- Obzedat, Ghost Council (Iconic Lore-Forward): Obzedat is the iconic old Orzhov power structure: deathless elites draining value, dodging consequences, and returning to collect again. Skip if: you need a fast engine or dislike high-mana commanders that win through slow drain. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/mm3/176/obzedat-ghost-council) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/obzedat-ghost-council)

## Adjacent Fits

- Yore / Artifice: Yore / Artifice appeared because you treated procedure as protection. Through Yore / Artifice, that pressure becomes engineered agency, artifice, civilization, technology.
- Black: Black stayed nearby because the self-sovereign operator pattern overlaps with the way your reading approached the table, then translates it into cost, agency, life payment, sacrifice.

name: Selesnya Conclave
decree: Selesnya Conclave recognizes the shape of your game as The Communal Harmonizer. Your answers repeatedly expressed careful stewardship and shared self. Ink / Altruism stayed near the reading, but Selesnya Conclave was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary guild fit.
hero: Selesnya read you as someone who trusts strength that is held together. White protects the bond; green lets it grow. Together, the deck makes a battlefield where the whole is more frightening than any single body. Ink / Altruism stayed close because your answers also carried protected public abundance, open knowledge, community benefit, guarded generosity, and clear separation from Black-style private control. The deciding difference was how Selesnya turns that pressure into collective momentum, shared growth, and combat math that multiplies.
reading_signal: Selesnya Conclave led with a moderate signal. A secondary signal stayed close: Ink / Altruism suggested protected public abundance, open knowledge, community benefit, guarded generosity, and clear separation from Black-style private control, while this result centered community, protection, and shared growth. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves outward into belonging and scale.

# Selesnya Conclave Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Selesnya Conclave

**Tagline:** A communal voice rooted in nature and shared purpose.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 4, B: 2, R: 4, G: 10

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The whole chord - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Selesnya Conclave and Five-Color / WUBRG.
- Signal 2: Steward the change - You let memory become stewardship, carrying the living house without turning duty into nostalgia. It echoed Selesnya Conclave and White.
- Signal 3: Belonging that softens the self - You made room for the board to become stronger together than any single card alone. It was answered by Selesnya Conclave.
- Signal 4: Stand with the circle - You made room for the board to become stronger together than any single card alone. It was answered by Selesnya Conclave.

## Commander Path

Selesnya Conclave wants a Commander deck that builds safety through numbers: make tokens, grow the board together, and turn collective strength into attacks that survive one-for-one answers. Start with Convoke Community or Go-Wide Caretaking, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Tokens, Counters Matter.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Convoke, token makers, anthem effects, protection, and board-building engines that make the whole table calculate your community at once.

## Table Caution

Protect the engine, rebuild after wipes, and keep drawing cards so the table cannot answer every token wave.

## Archetypes

- Convoke Community: Use creatures working together as gameplay texture for shared labor and communal purpose.
- Go-Wide Caretaking: Build a board that feels like a protected community, while remembering tokens alone are not lore proof.
- Harmony And Preservation: Favor play patterns that express mutual care, protection, and shared purpose over individual glory.

adjacentFit.relationshipCopy: Both paths recognized the same tension, but they solve it differently. Witherbloom asks: "What must be spent so the living engine keeps working?" Glint asks: "What opening is worth feeding before order makes it harmless?" Witherbloom moves downward into essence, body, and exchange; Glint moves toward adaptive appetite, living pressure, and storm-fed growth.

# Witherbloom College Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Witherbloom College

**Tagline:** Study life and death as living essences.

**Mana alignment:** W: 2, U: 3, B: 10, R: 4, G: 7

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The cold pattern - You trusted a small edge to compound until the table could no longer ignore it. It echoed Witherbloom College and Black.
- Signal 2: Keep the whole covenant - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Witherbloom College and Five-Color / WUBRG.
- Signal 3: The life-death exchange - You were willing to turn the graveyard into a second hand. It was answered by Witherbloom College.
- Signal 4: Make it a debt - You made room for the board to become stronger together than any single card alone. It was answered by Orzhov Syndicate.

## Commander Path

Witherbloom College wants a Commander deck that treats life and death as one economy: spend life, feed Pests, drain the table, and use Infusion lines to turn biology into power. Start with Essence Exchange or Remedies and Poisons, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Sacrifice, Lifegain.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Infusion, Pest sacrifice, drain engines, life gain, and metabolic loops that make healing and harm fuel the same Commander plan.

## Table Caution

Protect the drain engine, buy time with life gain, and rebuild through Pests when the table removes your outlet.

## Archetypes

- Essence Exchange: Life gain, life loss, Pests, sacrifice, healing, harm, and death triggers are Witherbloom signals when they express embodied life/death exchange.
- Remedies and Poisons: Brewing, medicine, toxicology, and mortuary practice show Witherbloom when they turn living essence into practical craft.
- Field Biology and Cost: Witherbloom becomes clearest when biological, ecological, or body-level evidence matters more than abstract proof alone.

name: Boros Legion
decree: Boros Legion recognizes the shape of your game as The Protective Intervener. Your answers repeatedly expressed felt ignition and preserving duty. White stayed near the reading, but Boros Legion was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary guild fit.
hero: Boros did not read you as a passive defender. It read you as someone who moves when the line is crossed. White gives the instinct to protect the table, the team, or the principle. Red gives the spark that refuses to wait. Together, that becomes righteous retaliation: a shield with fire behind it. White stayed close because your answers also carried safety, duty, and standards that hold under pressure. The deciding difference was how Boros turns that pressure into coordinated pressure, righteous retaliation, and visible action.
reading_signal: Boros Legion led with a moderate signal. A secondary signal stayed close: White suggested safety, duty, and standards that hold under pressure, while this result centered protection, grievance, and immediate action. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves outward into intervention.

rendered_text:
# Boros Legion Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Boros Legion

**Tagline:** Public protection. Disciplined action.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 3, B: 1, R: 9, G: 2

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The live spark - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Boros Legion and Red.
- Signal 2: Preserve what must not break - You trusted patience that keeps the next generation alive after the first pressure breaks. It echoed Boros Legion and White.
- Signal 3: Move now - You chose clean answers, patient sequencing, and a table where every spell has to earn its place. It was answered by Boros Legion.
- Signal 4: Wait for the living signal - You preferred making the table answer you before comfort became a plan. It was answered by Temur Frontier.

## Commander Path

Boros Legion wants a Commander deck that turns attacks into clean decisions: build one disciplined combat line, protect it, and use equipment or coordinated pressure to end hesitation. Start with Go-Wide Aggro or Burn / Heroic, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Tokens, Equipment.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Equipment, Battalion and Mentor-style pressure, protection, combat tricks, and efficient removal that reward tactical attacks over chaos.

## Table Caution

Sequence attacks carefully, protect your key threat, and remove the blocker that makes the clean strike fail.

## Archetypes

- Go-Wide Aggro: Raise the Alarm, Legion's Landing, Rally the Peasants. Flood the board with tokens and win through an alpha strike.
- Burn / Heroic: Monastery Swiftspear and Goblin Guide backed by Lightning Bolt and Boros Charm - the fastest possible clock.
- Equipment Voltron: Sram and Puresteel Paladin draw cards off every equipment, closing games with one overwhelming threat.

## Card Signals

name: Azorius Senate
decree: Azorius Senate recognizes the shape of your game as The Institutional Stabilizer. Your answers repeatedly expressed balanced chord and careful stewardship. White stayed near the reading, but Azorius Senate was the stronger match. This is a Vox Mana interpretive placement for a commander start, not an objective diagnosis or official canon.
result_status: This is your primary guild fit.
hero: Azorius read you as someone who protects the table by defining what is allowed to happen. White supplies the standard; blue supplies timing, documentation, and restraint. Together, the deck becomes law made playable: patient, exacting, and difficult to slip past. White stayed close because your answers also carried safety, duty, and standards that hold under pressure. The deciding difference was how Azorius turns that pressure into restricted action, procedural pressure, and clean enforcement.
reading_signal: Azorius Senate led with a moderate signal. A secondary signal stayed close: White suggested safety, duty, and standards that hold under pressure, while this result centered procedure, restraint, and enforceable standards. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves upward into order and precedent.

White asks: "What structure still protects people when goodwill is not enough?" Azorius moves upward into order and precedent; White moves upward into shelter and enforceable duty.

rendered_text:
# Azorius Senate Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Azorius Senate

**Tagline:** Law, procedure, and enforceable structure protect civic order when they stay accountable to the people they govern.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 9, B: 1, R: 2, G: 2

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The whole chord - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Azorius Senate and Five-Color / WUBRG.
- Signal 2: Steward the change - You let memory become stewardship, carrying the living house without turning duty into nostalgia. It echoed Azorius Senate and White.
- Signal 3: Follow the process - You chose clean answers, patient sequencing, and a table where every spell has to earn its place. It was answered by Azorius Senate.
- Signal 4: Convert the hidden leverage - You kept value in what the table could not yet see. It was answered by Sultai Brood.

## Commander Path

Azorius Senate wants a Commander deck that turns order into inevitability: keep mana open, tax greedy lines, and let rule-setting permanents decide which spells matter. Start with Draw-Go Control or Prison Control, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Midrange, Control, Tempo.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Countermagic, sweepers, tempo enforcement, detain effects, and taxation pieces that make the table play through law instead of impulse.

## Table Caution

Wait for the spell that breaks parity, hold interaction, and remove the key piece before the table slips around your rules.

## Archetypes

- Draw-Go Control: Hold up mana every turn. Counter threats at instant speed. Win with one resilient finisher after the opponent exhausts their resources.
- Prison Control: Deploy asymmetric restrictions - Thalia, Detention Sphere, Rule of Law - that prevent opponents from executing their game plan.
- Tempo / Spirits: Flash threats and counterspells in the same turn. Deploy a creature, protect it, answer opposition with open mana.

## Card Signals

### Creatures

- Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
- Lavinia of the Tenth
- Aven Mindcensor

### Instants and Sorceries

### Basic mana note
Tune Plains and Islands to your early pips after the nonbasic shell, ramp package, and utility lands are chosen.

## Commander Browsing Notes

- Isperia, Supreme Judge (Native Fit): Directly represents the guild's leadership and punishes those who dare attack the law (you). Skip if: You prefer a proactive, aggressive strategy rather than reactive defense. - Lavinia, Azorius Renegade (Iconic Lore-Forward): A major modern Azorius figure whose gameplay keeps opponents from bypassing normal spell costs and mana constraints. Skip if: You are playing in a casual meta where players don't rely on mana rocks or free spells. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/rvr/195/lavinia-azorius-renegade) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/lavinia-azorius-renegade)
- Grand Arbiter Augustin IV (Advanced): The ultimate expression of Azorius tax-based gameplay; he slows the game down to a crawl. Skip if: Your playgroup dislikes 'Stax' or games that take 3+ hours. [Scryfall](https://scryfall.com/card/2x2/221/grand-arbiter-augustin-iv) / [EDHREC](https://edhrec.com/commanders/grand-arbiter-augustin-iv)

decree: Five-Color / WUBRG recognizes the shape of your game as The Full-Spectrum Integrator. Your answers repeatedly expressed balanced chord and integrated covenant. result_status: This is your primary five-color fit.
hero: Five-Color read your answers as a table where all five voices were present. White asked for structure, Blue for understanding, Black for agency, Red for motion, and Green for belonging. Orzhov Syndicate stayed close because your answers also carried obligation, debt, and consequence. The deciding difference was how Five-Color turns that pressure into full color access, deliberate fixing, many kinds of answers, and a plan that keeps breadth from becoming drift.

A secondary signal stayed close: Orzhov Syndicate suggested obligation, debt, and consequence, while this result centered all five colors present, full-spectrum integration, coalition, color breadth, and tradeoffs that keep access from becoming goodstuff. The deciding difference was motion: this result chose the path that moves toward all-five-color synthesis and full-spectrum Commander expression.

# Five-Color / WUBRG Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Five-Color / WUBRG

**Tagline:** Every color present. Every shortcut questioned.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 10, B: 10, R: 10, G: 10

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The whole chord - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Five-Color / WUBRG and Bant.
- Signal 2: Keep the whole covenant - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Five-Color / WUBRG and Bant.
- Signal 3: Every color has a job - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It was answered by Five-Color / WUBRG.
- Signal 4: Make the debt visible - You counted every exchange, then made the table pay for thinking it was even. It was answered by Orzhov Syndicate.

## Commander Path

Five-Color / WUBRG wants a Commander deck that uses all five colors deliberately: build reliable fixing, decide what each color contributes, and keep support-only Commander examples from becoming lore, legality, or ranking proof. Start from the Full-Spectrum Integrator or Coalition Builder lane, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Five-Color, Ramp, Multicolor.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Domain, converge, sunburst, WUBRG costs or activations, multicolor payoffs, basic-land-type checks, and mana infrastructure can express Five-Color texture while individual card claims remain manually verified.

## Table Caution

Develop fixing with a purpose, make every color justify its slot, and treat precons, MTGDecks, Archidekt, and Scryfall links as support navigation rather than proof.

## Archetypes

- Full-Spectrum Integrator: Uses every color because the problem needs every mode of answer, not because every card is automatically welcome.
- Coalition Builder: Turns difference into a working table where structure, insight, agency, motion, and belonging can each matter.
- Boundary Keeper: Refuses to let five-color breadth become superiority, Colorless proof, four-color leakage, or unsupported Commander claims.

decree: Yore / Artifice recognizes the shape of your game as The Engineered Agency Architect. Your answers repeatedly expressed preserving duty and engineered agency against finality. hero: Rewrite the limit. Keep the engine honest. Yore reads your answers as a four-color without Green machine of agency. # Yore / Artifice Commander Dossier

**Dossier type:** Primary

**Expression name:** Yore / Artifice

**Tagline:** Rewrite the limit. Keep the engine honest.

**Mana alignment:** W: 10, U: 10, B: 10, R: 10, G: 1

## Signals From Your Answers

- Signal 1: The whole chord - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It echoed Yore / Artifice and Five-Color / WUBRG.
- Signal 2: Preserve what must not break - You trusted patience that keeps the next generation alive after the first pressure breaks. It echoed Yore / Artifice and White.
- Signal 3: Build the agency machine - You chose the line that made the table reveal itself before you committed your best card. It was answered by Yore / Artifice.
- Signal 4: The machine refuses surrender - You were willing to turn the graveyard into a second hand. It was answered by Yore / Artifice.

## Commander Path

Yore / Artifice wants a Commander deck that turns artifacts, sacrifice, recursion, and controlled engines into table texture for engineered agency against natural surrender. Start with Engineered Agency or Artifice And Archive, then tune the 99 so your best turns feel like your reading did.

## Deck Footing

Budget and experience: mid budget, returning pilot. Your first searches should orbit Artifacts, Aristocrats, Control.

## Spellcraft / Gameplay Identity

Use artifacts, sacrifice, recursion, control, value engines, and precise combo texture as Commander-facing ways to show artifice and constructed continuity. They are table texture, not the source of the name or identity.

## Table Caution

Build the engine carefully, protect the piece that keeps agency online, and avoid treating every artifact or graveyard line as Yore unless it carries the four-color without Green worldview.

## Archetypes

- Engineered Agency: Builds systems that let structure, knowledge, ambition, and heat push past natural surrender.
- Artifice And Archive: Turns tools, records, costs, and memories into machinery for a future that can still be chosen.
- Controlled Overreach: Carries the shadow risk of treating every limit as raw material.
